newsitem.title: PERU: Peru Jan-Feb oil deficit rises 49 pct on 1996.
newsitem.headline: Peru Jan-Feb oil deficit rises 49 pct on 1996.

text.p: Peru posted an oil and derivatives deficit of $71 million in the first two months of the year, up 49 percent from $48 million in the same period 1996, said the Central Bank Tuesday.
The bank's weekly report also showed a $30 million deficit in February compared with a $17 million deficit in the same month last year.
Imports rose 22.5 percent in the first two months of the year to $133 million, from $109 million in the same period 1996.
Exports edged up 2.3 percent in the January-February period to $62 million from $61 million in the same two months last year.
Peru imported oil and derivatives worth $54 million in February, a rise of 32 percent against February 1996.
Exports grew 24 percent in February to $39 million from $20 million in the same month last year.
Peru reported an oil deficit of $347 million last year, up 11 percent on the previous year.
